label: digit 1 input at early steps (t=2-4)
explanation: Fires almost only when the input token is the digit 1 at step t=2, 3 or 4 (94% of activation mass on in_tok=1). This is mostly the original phase (t=3 strongest, about 61% of mass; t=2 about 27%). The largest activations come from L=3 sequences that start with 1: at t=4 the copied-back first token 1 is the input (recall_idx 1), and precision there is 0.93. It never fires at t<2 or t>=5, never on the delimiter, and almost never on other tokens (small leftovers on j/z/m). Precision is low (about 0.24): only about a quarter of 1-at-t=2..4 steps fire, and which ones fire depends diffusely on the earlier tokens (prev_tok in {2,d,l,w,k,b,g,s} lifts F1 to 0.49). I could not find a clean rule for that context dependence. Magnitude is highest for copy-phase t=4 in L=3 sequences and next highest at original t=3.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=1 (+5.49), t=2 & in_tok=1 (+4.28), in_tok=j (+3.65), in_tok=z (+3.57), in_tok=m (+3.17), t=3 & in_tok=1 (+2.66). Lower it: prev_tok=m (-3.79), prev2_tok=m (-3.67), prev_tok=0 (-3.26), prev_tok=x (-3.16).
